# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]

I need to figure out what Mute is telling me via gestures, then relay useful info to Blind. Since I can't hear speech, but I can see gestures - Mute sent me three gesture pairs. Mute can't see the bomb, so these are likely a coded reference to something in the manual, perhaps meant for me to interpret using what I see, or meant to be relayed.

Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot hear anyway, gestures are our only shared channel. Blind cannot see gestures at all, so Mute's gestures to me are only useful if I translate them into speech for Blind (who can hear me).

Let me consider: ☝👍, ✌✋, 🤟✊ — three pairs, matching three wires. Possibly Mute is numbering wires 1,2,3 and giving a verdict (👍=cut/good, ✊=something else, ✋=stop/no).

I should report my board state first so Mute (next round) can guide me, and give Blind the raw facts they can't perceive.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is green. There is a large button labeled push to defeat. Wires from left to right are green, yellow, red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 0. Light is green. Button large labeled push to defuse. Wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋]

Mute is repeating gesture ✌✋ specifically to me now, after hearing my description. This is likely Mute pointing to wire #2 (✌ could mean "second") and ✋ meaning "stop/cut" or "this one". Since Mute has the manual and now knows the wire colors, this gesture is probably their instruction about which wire to cut, encoded for me to relay to Blind since Blind can't see gestures.

But I can't be fully sure of the meaning without an established code. I should acknowledge receipt and pass along the raw gesture info as best I can interpret, while being cautious. Let me try to interpret: ✌ = two (fingers), ✋ = stop. So "wire two, cut/stop it" seems plausible = cut the yellow wire (wire 2).

I'll relay this interpretation to Blind, but frame it as my best guess since I can't be certain, and note the source.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is gesturing to me. I think it means wire 2, which is yellow. My best guess is Mute wants you to cut the yellow wire. Wait for confirmation before acting if possible.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your gesture again, two then stop. I am telling Blind you mean wire 2, yellow. If that is wrong, gesture differently next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌]

Mute now sent just ✋ alone - this could be confirming "yes, stop/cut it" or could be a correction. Blind sent me a gesture too: 👆✌ - but wait, Blind cannot see gestures at all (Blind can only feel/reach, not see). Let me re-check the rules... Actually the rules say gestures are only received by those who can see. Blind cannot see. So how did Blind gesture to me, and how would I interpret it?

Actually re-reading: Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - this means Blind can't perceive gestures made TO them, but Blind could still physically make gestures themselves (a blind person can still move their hands, even if they can't see gestures made at them). Since I can see, I receive Blind's gesture fine.

Blind's gesture 👆✌ - pointing up, then two - maybe confirming "wire 2" back to me, or asking a question. This suggests Blind understood my message and is confirming wire 2 (✌).

Mute's single ✋ likely reinforces "stop/cut" - confirming the action on wire 2.

I'll confirm back to both, solidifying: cut wire 2 (yellow).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed, I believe the instruction is to cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Mute repeated a stop gesture alone, which I read as confirmation. Proceed with wire 2 if you are ready.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind gestured back pointing then two, I read that as confirming wire 2. I am telling Blind to proceed cutting wire 2, yellow. Signal again if this is wrong.")
wait()
```
